grades: Completion of incomplete and unreported grades

An incomplete requires passing/good standing, at least half the work completed, unusual circumstances and an agreed completion deadline no later than one year; the grade-key rule also requires completion before graduation, whichever is earlier, subject to authorized extension. Unfinished I/IP/NG grades have the source-stated IF/F conversion rules and do not independently supply earned credit. An ordinary D earns credit but may not satisfy a major or a higher course-specific minimum.
Credit-only grade-key wording and specific conversion policy

The grade key describes CR as credit based on a C average or better and NC as below C. The separately registered Course Information CR/NC section explicitly includes C-minus among grades converted to CR. Both published statements are retained; the precise C-minus boundary needs university clarification if material to an individual free elective. Neither wording permits present major/minor/general-education requirements to be elected credit-only.
business: Business written exceptions and published changes

Students must comply with the Bulletin and written changes to their program. Deviations from department, program or school requirements need written approval from the Associate Dean or, in specified cases, the relevant department chair. The school may change offerings, minimum grades or GPAs and communicate changes by written/electronic notice or advising. No waiver or immutable student-cohort assignment is inferred.

This applies only to a readmission request. A previously academically dismissed student or one with cumulative GPA below 2.0 must show changed conditions and a reasonable prospect of satisfactory performance. Nonacademic dismissal requires written Dean of Students authorization. A Business student who did not earn at least C in MAS110 or MTH161 will not be readmitted. Readmission may carry additional conditions; outside study after the last Miami enrollment requires transcripts from all attended institutions for review. This C threshold does not replace the ordinary degree table C-minus rule for a continuously enrolled student.
arts: Arts and Sciences exemptions and credit distinction

The college distinguishes accepted AP/IB credit by examination, placement by proficiency/test scores without earned credit, and advanced standing/placement with credit. Exemption does not automatically supply credits or waive a program-specific amount. Existing written departmental approval, language-waiver and total-degree rules remain separate.
